name: Total population
methodology: Total enumerated population per the decadal Census of India; intercensal years use official projections where published.

name: Sex ratio
methodology: Number of females per 1,000 males in the enumerated population, per the Census of India.

name: Urban population share
methodology: Share of population living in areas classified urban by the Census of India.

name: Literacy rate
methodology: Share of persons aged 7 and above able to read and write with understanding, per Census of India / NSO literacy surveys.

name: Gross enrolment ratio (secondary)
methodology: Enrolment at the NEP 2020 Secondary stage (Classes IX to XII) as a share of the corresponding age-group population, total of boys and girls, per UDISE+ (Ministry of Education).

name: Pupil-teacher ratio (elementary)
methodology: Enrolled pupils per teacher at the elementary stage, per UDISE+.

name: Gross State Domestic Product
methodology: GSDP at current prices as published by MoSPI / state economic surveys. Base-year revisions break comparability across series; note the base year.

name: Per capita income
methodology: Per capita Net State Domestic Product at current prices, per MoSPI.

name: Fiscal deficit
methodology: Gross fiscal deficit as a share of GSDP, per RBI's annual State Finances: A Study of Budgets.

name: Unemployment rate
methodology: Unemployment rate (usual status) for persons aged 15+, per the Periodic Labour Force Survey (NSO).

name: Infant mortality rate
methodology: Infant deaths per 1,000 live births, per the Sample Registration System (Registrar General of India).

name: Life expectancy at birth
methodology: Expectation of life at birth, per SRS abridged life tables.

name: Government hospital beds
methodology: Beds in government hospitals per lakh population, per the National Health Profile (CBHI).

name: Household toilet coverage
methodology: Share of households with access to a toilet facility, per Census of India / NFHS / Swachh Bharat Mission reporting; sources differ in definition, note which.

name: Household electrification
methodology: Share of households using electricity as primary lighting source, per Census of India / Saubhagya dashboard.

name: Total road length
methodology: Total road length maintained by all agencies, per Basic Road Statistics of India (MoRTH).

name: Internet subscribers
methodology: Internet subscribers per 100 population, per TRAI performance indicator reports (licensed service area mapped to state).

name: Foodgrain production
methodology: Total foodgrain production, per Agricultural Statistics at a Glance (Ministry of Agriculture).

name: Irrigated area
methodology: Net irrigated area as a share of net sown area, per Land Use Statistics (Ministry of Agriculture).

name: Annual rainfall
methodology: Actual annual rainfall for the meteorological subdivision, per the India Meteorological Department.

name: Forest cover
methodology: Forest cover as a share of geographical area, per the biennial India State of Forest Report (Forest Survey of India).

name: Protected areas
methodology: Number of national parks and wildlife sanctuaries, per the Wildlife Institute of India / ENVIS.

name: Cognizable crime rate
methodology: Cognizable IPC crimes registered per lakh population, per NCRB Crime in India. Registration rates vary by state; higher figures can reflect better registration.

name: Crimes against women
methodology: Crimes against women registered per lakh female population, per NCRB Crime in India; the registration caveat applies.

name: Road accident deaths
methodology: Persons killed in road accidents, per MoRTH Road Accidents in India.

name: Total fertility rate
methodology: Average number of children expected to be born per woman over her reproductive span at current age-specific fertility rates, per SRS Statistical Reports (Registrar General of India).

name: Unemployment rate (rural)
methodology: Unemployed per 1,000 persons in the rural labour force, usual status (adjusted), per NSSO Employment-Unemployment Surveys and PLFS. The survey changed to PLFS from 2017-18; earlier and later figures are not strictly comparable.

name: Unemployment rate (urban)
methodology: Unemployed per 1,000 persons in the urban labour force, usual status (adjusted), per NSSO Employment-Unemployment Surveys and PLFS. The survey changed to PLFS from 2017-18; earlier and later figures are not strictly comparable.

name: Steel capacity, operating
methodology: Sum of current capacity over Indian steelmaking furnace units with status operating or operating pre-retirement, across electric arc, basic oxygen, induction and open hearth routes. Snapshot at the named release, not a historical series: the tracker records each unit's current capacity, and start years are unknown for most Indian units, so no year-by-year reconstruction is published. The tracker covers only plants of 0.5 million tonnes per annum and greater, so small plants are outside these totals. Source: Global Energy Monitor, Global Iron and Steel Tracker, June 2026 (V1) release, CC BY 4.0.

name: Steel capacity, under construction
methodology: Sum of current capacity over Indian steelmaking furnace units with status construction. Snapshot at the named release, not a historical series: the tracker records each unit's current capacity, and start years are unknown for most Indian units, so no year-by-year reconstruction is published. The tracker covers only plants of 0.5 million tonnes per annum and greater, so small plants are outside these totals. Source: Global Energy Monitor, Global Iron and Steel Tracker, June 2026 (V1) release, CC BY 4.0.

name: Steel capacity, announced
methodology: Sum of current capacity over Indian steelmaking furnace units with status announced. Announced projects may never be built. Snapshot at the named release, not a historical series: the tracker records each unit's current capacity, and start years are unknown for most Indian units, so no year-by-year reconstruction is published. The tracker covers only plants of 0.5 million tonnes per annum and greater, so small plants are outside these totals. Source: Global Energy Monitor, Global Iron and Steel Tracker, June 2026 (V1) release, CC BY 4.0.

name: Steel capacity, operating, electric arc route
methodology: Sum of current capacity over Indian electric arc furnace units with status operating or operating pre-retirement. Snapshot at the named release, not a historical series: the tracker records each unit's current capacity, and start years are unknown for most Indian units, so no year-by-year reconstruction is published. The tracker covers only plants of 0.5 million tonnes per annum and greater, so small plants are outside these totals. Source: Global Energy Monitor, Global Iron and Steel Tracker, June 2026 (V1) release, CC BY 4.0.

name: Steel capacity, operating, basic oxygen route
methodology: Sum of current capacity over Indian basic oxygen furnace units with status operating or operating pre-retirement. Snapshot at the named release, not a historical series: the tracker records each unit's current capacity, and start years are unknown for most Indian units, so no year-by-year reconstruction is published. The tracker covers only plants of 0.5 million tonnes per annum and greater, so small plants are outside these totals. Source: Global Energy Monitor, Global Iron and Steel Tracker, June 2026 (V1) release, CC BY 4.0.

name: Steel capacity, operating, induction route
methodology: Sum of current capacity over Indian induction furnace units with status operating or operating pre-retirement. Snapshot at the named release, not a historical series: the tracker records each unit's current capacity, and start years are unknown for most Indian units, so no year-by-year reconstruction is published. The tracker covers only plants of 0.5 million tonnes per annum and greater, so small plants are outside these totals. Source: Global Energy Monitor, Global Iron and Steel Tracker, June 2026 (V1) release, CC BY 4.0.

name: Steel capacity, nominal crude, operating plants
methodology: Sum of nominal crude steel capacity over GEM-tracked Indian plants with status operating or operating pre-retirement, attributed to the state of the plant. Plant-level nominal capacity; the archive's unit-level steel indicators sum individual tracked furnaces instead, so the two measures differ and neither is adjusted toward the other. The tracker covers only plants of 0.5 million tonnes per annum and greater. Snapshot at the named release. Source: Global Energy Monitor, Global Iron and Steel Tracker, June 2026 (V1) release, CC BY 4.0.

name: Cement capacity, operating
methodology: Sum of cement capacity over GEM-tracked Indian cement plants with status operating, attributed to the state of the plant, per the tracker's own inclusion criteria. Snapshot at the named release, not a historical series. Source: Global Energy Monitor, Global Cement and Concrete Tracker, July 2026 (V1) release, CC BY 4.0.

name: Metallurgical coal mined
methodology: Country-level metallurgical coal production, estimated by GEM by summing mine-level production, using mine capacity where production is unknown. The file's consumption columns are factor-based estimates and are not published here. Snapshot for the release period. Source: Global Energy Monitor, Production and Consumption of Met Coal and Iron Ore by Steel Industry, December 2025 (V1) release, CC BY 4.0.

name: Iron ore mined
methodology: Country-level iron ore production, estimated by GEM by summing mine-level production, applying a 45 percent utilization rate to capacity where production is unknown. The file's consumption columns are factor-based estimates and are not published here. Snapshot for the release period. Source: Global Energy Monitor, Production and Consumption of Met Coal and Iron Ore by Steel Industry, December 2025 (V1) release, CC BY 4.0.

name: Pig iron produced
methodology: Country-level pig iron production as reported by the World Steel Association, with GEM blast furnace capacity used where WSA production is unknown. The file's consumption columns are factor-based estimates and are not published here. Snapshot for the release period. Source: Global Energy Monitor, Production and Consumption of Met Coal and Iron Ore by Steel Industry, December 2025 (V1) release, CC BY 4.0.

name: Direct reduced iron produced
methodology: Country-level DRI production as reported by the World Steel Association, with GEM DRI capacity used where WSA production is unknown. The file's consumption columns are factor-based estimates and are not published here. Snapshot for the release period. Source: Global Energy Monitor, Production and Consumption of Met Coal and Iron Ore by Steel Industry, December 2025 (V1) release, CC BY 4.0.

name: Utility-scale solar capacity, operating
methodology: Cumulative nameplate capacity of utility-scale solar projects, being those of 1 MW and above, with status operating, summed over the projects whose recorded commissioning year is the stated year or earlier. Of 3743 operating Indian projects 3570 carry a commissioning year, being 92,753.8 MW of 99,357.3 MW (93.4 per cent of operating capacity); the undated remainder is absent from every year, so each value understates the fleet by that much. Global Energy Monitor records capacity as either an alternating-current rating or a direct-current peak rating and frequently does not state which: of operating Indian capacity 51.7 per cent is stated MWac, 20.6 per cent MWp/dc and 27.7 per cent unspecified. The ratings are summed as published and are not converted between bases. The series is reconstructed from the fleet operating at the release date, so a project commissioned and later retired does not appear; the source records no retired Indian projects. Records for 2575 Indian projects derive partly or wholly from the TransitionZero Solar Asset Mapper, distributed under CC BY-NC 4.0, and 621 from the wiki-solar.org dataset.

name: Utility-scale wind capacity, operating
methodology: Cumulative nameplate capacity of wind projects with status operating, summed over the projects whose recorded commissioning year is the stated year or earlier. The tracker's global threshold excludes wind farms below 10 MW, so small installations are outside the series entirely. COVERAGE IS PARTIAL: of 679 operating Indian projects only 403 carry a commissioning year, being 27,055.4 MW of 38,937 MW (69.5 per cent of operating capacity). Every value therefore understates installed wind capacity, and the latest value should not be read as India's wind total. The undated share is spread across states rather than concentrated in the earliest ones, so the shape of the series is less affected than its level. Every dated project carries a state, so the state values sum to the national one. The series is reconstructed from the fleet operating at the release date, so a project commissioned and later retired does not appear; the source records no retired Indian projects.

name: Ironmaking capacity, blast furnace route, operating
methodology: Sum of current capacity over Indian blast furnaces, which reduce iron ore with coke to make pig iron, with status operating or operating pre-retirement, as at the June 2026 (V1) release. Covers 94 units, every one of which is located by joining the unit workbook to the plant-level workbook on GEM plant ID; the unit sheets carry no state of their own. This measures IRONMAKING and is a different quantity from the steelmaking capacity published from the same tracker, which is neither corrected toward this nor derived from it. No year-by-year series is published even though the workbook records a start year for each unit: the capacity figure is a present-day rating, the oldest operating unit dates from 1919, and every dated operating Indian unit carries a recorded relining, so attributing today's rating to the year a furnace first lit would state a figure the source does not support.

name: Ironmaking capacity, direct reduced iron route, operating
methodology: Sum of current capacity over Indian direct reduced iron furnaces, which reduce iron ore without melting it, with status operating or operating pre-retirement, as at the June 2026 (V1) release. Covers 222 units, every one of which is located by joining the unit workbook to the plant-level workbook on GEM plant ID; the unit sheets carry no state of their own. This measures IRONMAKING and is a different quantity from the steelmaking capacity published from the same tracker, which is neither corrected toward this nor derived from it. No year-by-year series is published even though the workbook records a start year for each unit: the capacity figure is a present-day rating, the oldest operating unit dates from 1990, and a unit's rating can change over its life while the workbook keeps only the current figure, with the start year missing for a fifth of operating capacity.

name: Hydropower capacity, operating
methodology: Cumulative nameplate capacity of hydropower projects with status operating, summed over the projects whose recorded commissioning year is the stated year or earlier. Conventional storage, run-of-river and pumped storage are counted together; pumped storage consumes more electricity than it returns and is a store rather than a source, so a total that includes it is not a generation figure. All 224 operating Indian projects carry a commissioning year and a state, covering 51,082 MW. The series is reconstructed from the fleet operating at the release date, so a project commissioned and later retired does not appear; the source records no retired Indian projects.

name: Nuclear capacity, operating
methodology: Cumulative nameplate capacity of nuclear reactor units with status operating, summed over the units whose recorded commissioning year is the stated year or earlier. The tracker applies no capacity threshold, so every tracked Indian reactor is included. All 21 operating Indian units carry a commissioning year and a state, covering 8,240 MW. Capacity is the gross nameplate rating; the workbook also carries design net and reference net capacity, which are smaller and are not what this series reports. The series is reconstructed from the fleet operating at the release date, so a unit commissioned and later retired does not appear; the source records no retired Indian units.

name: Gas and oil fired power capacity, operating
methodology: Cumulative capacity of power units burning fossil gas or fossil liquids, with status operating, summed over the units whose recorded commissioning year is the stated year or earlier. This is generating capacity, not generation: a gas or oil fired unit is typically run to follow demand rather than at a constant output, so capacity says what could be produced and not what was. Of 100 operating Indian units 91 carry a commissioning year, being 27,363.2 MW of 28,201.7 MW (97.0 per cent of operating capacity); the undated remainder is absent from every year. Every operating Indian unit carries a state, so the state values sum to the national one. Units burning more than one fuel are counted once at their full capacity under whichever fuels the source lists. The series is reconstructed from the fleet operating at the release date, so a unit commissioned and later retired does not appear; the source records 1 retired Indian unit, excluded here and absent from every year.

name: Iron ore mine design capacity, operating
methodology: Sum of design capacity over Indian iron ore mines with status operating, as at the August 2025 (V1) release. Covers 220 mines carrying a design capacity; 5 operating Indian mines record none and are excluded. Design capacity is what a mine is built to produce, not what it produced. The workbook's own production columns for 2022, 2023 and 2024 are NOT published here: they are reported by 177, 163 and 126 Indian mines respectively, so a series across them would show the number of reporting mines changing and read as production changing. No year-by-year capacity series is published either, because design capacity is a present-day rating and attributing it to the year a mine opened would state a figure the source does not support.

name: Coal fired power capacity, operating
methodology: Cumulative capacity of coal fired power units with status operating, summed over the units whose recorded commissioning year is the stated year or earlier. Taken from the integrated tracker rather than a coal-specific one; the same file's wind and nuclear rows reproduce the dedicated trackers exactly, which is why the other technologies are not read from it. Of 862 operating Indian units 860 carry a commissioning year, being 254,317.7 MW of 254,432.7 MW (100.0 per cent of operating capacity); the undated remainder is absent from every year. Every operating Indian unit carries a state, so the state values sum to the national one. By steam cycle, 158,350.7 MW of operating capacity is subcritical and 90,210 MW supercritical or ultra-supercritical; the distinction is the source's own and is reported, not scored. This is generating capacity and not generation or emissions. The series is reconstructed from the fleet operating at the release date, so a unit commissioned and later retired does not appear; the source records 170 retired Indian units, excluded here and absent from every year.

name: Bioenergy power capacity, operating
methodology: Sum of capacity over Indian bioenergy power units with status operating, as at the August 2026 release. Covers 136 units totalling 2,746.8 MW, burning agricultural waste, wood, municipal and industrial refuse and paper mill wastes. No year-by-year series is published: only 58.6 per cent of that capacity carries a commissioning year, so a cumulative curve would understate the fleet by more than a third and would say more about what the source knows than about what was built. 50 MW sits in 4 units with no recorded state, which the national figure includes and no state figure does, so the state values do not sum to the national one.

name: Coal mine capacity, operating
methodology: Sum of capacity over Indian coal mines with status operating, as at the May 2026 release. Covers 349 mines; 16 operating Indian mines record no capacity and are excluded. This is what the mines are built to extract, not what they extracted. Two things in the workbook are deliberately not published: its production column, because each figure carries its own year of production rather than a common one, and any year-by-year series, because only 57.3 per cent of these mines record an opening year and capacity is a present-day rating that cannot be laid on the year a mine opened.
